name: What counts as a minor home repair versus a full remodel?

mainEntity.name: What counts as a minor home repair versus a full remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor home repairs include localized fixes that address everyday wear, damage, or minor failures without gutting a space. Common examples handled by HH Remodeling include patching damaged drywall, repairing interior trim and baseboards, fixing broken or loose floor tiles, touch-up painting, and securing loose cabinet hardware. Minor repairs also cover small wood rot fixes, door adjustments, and minor accessibility modifications. Major remodels involve structural changes, room additions, or complete tear-outs. If your project does not require altering load-bearing framing or reconfiguring major plumbing lines, it generally falls under minor repairs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Minor home repairs address localized issues like drywall patching, broken tile replacement, trim fixes, and touch-up painting without gutting or rebuilding entire living spaces.
